chunks.summary: Z-peak chi-square flagged (p=0.000229), survives BH correction, but Z-peak KS is clean (p=0.958) -- suggests localized bin irregularity, not a broad shift. Occupancy and full-spectrum tests all normal. Mean mass 90.478 GeV, mildly off-nominal.

[LATER FOUND TO BE A MEASUREMENT ARTIFACT, NOT REAL] Full-spectrum chi-square returned p=0.0 (stat~2,000,008) -- at the time interpreted as a catastrophic localized bin overflow. Subsequently traced to a chi_square_test bug: a single stray event in a reference-empty bin, combined with a one-sample-vs-two-sample statistical error, produced non-physical significance. See LAB_MANUAL.md / NOTES.md for the full writeup.
All tests clean after correction. Z-peak share is softer than expected (271 events, p=0.070, not significant) -- second chunk trending low, worth watching. Full-spectrum mean mass dropping.
[LATER FOUND TO BE A MEASUREMENT ARTIFACT] Full-spectrum chi-square p=0.0 again (2nd occurrence) -- see chunk_2 note. Z-peak mean mass drifting upward across 4 chunks: 90.478 -> 90.785 GeV.

REAL FINDING CONFIRMED: Z-peak occupancy drop (p=0.00086, 248 vs ~299 expected events) plus formal drift detection now active -- Z-peak mean mass risen monotonically across 5 chunks (90.478->91.030 GeV), drift z-score 3.55 sigma, slope +0.138 GeV/chunk. Total occupancy normal -- events migrating OUT of Z-peak window, not lost globally. Classic momentum-scale miscalibration signature.

5/6 tests now flagged. Z-peak shape (KS+chi2) both fail for the first time -- distortion now large enough to be a broad shift, not just bin-level. Z-peak mean mass crossed above nominal: 91.577 GeV (+0.387 above 91.19). Drift z-score 4.39 sigma, slope accelerating to +0.206 GeV/chunk.

Z-peak occupancy depletion worst yet: 227 events (15.1% share vs 19.9% reference, p=1.7e-6). Z-peak shape still failing. Mean mass 91.447 GeV, sustained above nominal. Sustained momentum-scale miscalibration.

Full-spectrum shape now also failing decisively (both KS and chi2) -- distortion large enough to deform the entire spectrum. Z-peak mean mass new high: 91.617 GeV (+0.427 above nominal). 5/6 tests failing.

[Full-spectrum chi2 p=0.0 is the measurement artifact -- see chunk_2 note] Z-peak mean mass jumps to 92.545 GeV, +1.355 above nominal -- single-chunk leap of +0.928 GeV. Z-peak shape p-values at the most extreme of the whole run (1.3e-33). Drift z-score re-spikes to 3.43 sigma, slope accelerating to +0.234 GeV/chunk.

[Full-spectrum chi2 p=0.0 is the measurement artifact] Z-peak mean mass new record: 92.702 GeV (+1.512 above nominal). Z-peak shape p-values set new records (chi2 p=6.4e-37). Drift slope +0.253 GeV/chunk, accelerating.

[Full-spectrum chi2 p=0.0 is the measurement artifact] Z-peak chi-square statistic more than doubled in one chunk (193.9 -> 414.8, p=9.5e-84) -- most extreme of the run. Z-peak mean mass 93.541 GeV, +2.351 above nominal. Drift slope steepest yet: +0.290 GeV/chunk.

[Full-spectrum chi2 p=0.0 is the measurement artifact] NEW: total occupancy collapse -- only 827/1500 events (z=-17.4 sigma) -- this is the final, smaller, partial chunk (real data ran out), not a real DAQ failure. Z-peak mean mass 93.845 GeV, +2.655 above nominal, steepest drift slope of the run (+0.312 GeV/chunk).
